subject: %Phenotypic variance explained by a QTL after non parametric interval mapping

messages.author: b851f9a8b81a6867
messages.subject: %Phenotypic variance explained by a QTL after non parametric interval mapping
parts:
Hi Dr Carl

I am working on mapping non normal phenotypes (rank based). So, I am using non parametric interval mapping codes for the analysis. 
I was going through the fitqtl function for estimating the percent phenotypic variance explained by a qtl and found that there are only 2 options for the model. Do you think I should use binary as the model for my case or normal? 

fitqtl(cross, pheno.col=1, qtl, covar=NULL, formula, method=c("imp", "hk"),
       model=c("normal", "binary"), dropone=TRUE, get.ests=FALSE, 
       run.checks=TRUE, tol=1e-4, maxit=1000)

Thanks
Raghu

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] %Phenotypic variance explained by a QTL after non parametric interval mapping
parts:
The binary model is appropriate only if the phenotype has two values, 0 and 1. But in that case, the non-parametric interval mapping approach would not be appropriate. I would use model="normal", but I would be cautious in interpreting the results.

karl
